biteCue.audio: Two-tone WebAudio beep, 880 Hz then 1320 Hz, 90 ms each; no audio asset, plays when the bite starts.
biteCue.haptic: Vibration pattern [60, 40, 60] ms; one 30 ms pulse in low-memory mode.
biteCue.visual: Amber BITE! banner (#ffb703) with a pulsing animation; static in low-memory mode.

firstQuestWindowMs.note: Forgiving first-quest window (VEX 5.0 item 2): while the player is on quest 1 or 2 the bite window is 1800 ms and the hookset window is 1200 ms, so a first-time player succeeds most big bites without it feeling automatic. From quest 3 the per-size windows above apply. The first-attempt grace period still adds on top.

Cedar Creek.note: First legend most players meet; mid difficulty.

Ember Lake.note: Hardest legend: fastest drift and fastest fight ticks.

Millpond.note: Easiest legend: slowest drift, most generous reel gain.

missPenalty.description: Missing a hookset spooks the fish: the line goes slack for 8 seconds and that spot will not bite again for 30 seconds. No coins or tackle are lost.

note: All bite/hookset numbers live here, not in code. Tune from real-phone playtest logs (src/playtest.js), never from a guess.

performance.note: Devices reporting navigator.deviceMemory at or below lowMemoryGB run in low-memory mode: one short haptic pulse instead of a pattern, and no pulsing bite-cue animation. In low-memory mode the idle line also waits a fixed lowMemoryIdleDelayMs between bites (instead of the normal 4-9 s random gap) and the fight bar ticks at lowMemoryFightTickMs instead of 120 ms, so a low-end Android 6.0-8 phone does less work per second during the busiest moments. Crashes are logged with device RAM in src/playtest.js so low-memory shutdowns can be reproduced by device.

fast.note: For confident players: more bites, less time to hookset.

slow.biteChance: fewer bites — fish take their time
slow.note: For new players and legends: more time to react, fewer chances.

retrieveSpeedTradeoff.status: Stated trade-off (VEX 5.0 item 7). The retrieve selector UI ships with the milestone-4 tackle shop; until then the game fishes at the medium baseline.

pacing.note: Design targets for the 12-quest arc (VEX 5.0 follow-up, suggestion 497): pacing, economy and difficulty tuning, written down so repetition and burnout can be checked against numbers instead of a feeling. These are TARGETS, not measurements — the real 1–12 playthrough (docs/quests.md pacing log) is still empty; retune from it when it exists.
pacing.arcTarget: Quests 1–2 inside the first 10 minutes (first session, first hand-fought catch included); quests 3–5 inside the first hour; first legend (Silver King, quest 8) in session 2; full 1–12 arc across 3–5 sessions, about 2–3 hours total.

idleGapMs.note: Idle-line gap between bites, as shipped in main.js scheduleIdleBite (low-memory mode uses the fixed lowMemoryIdleDelayMs instead). At the 60% auto-catch rate this is about one idle fish every ~11 s, ~5–6 fish a minute, ~25–30 coins a minute from the idle line alone.

difficultyRamp.note: Multiplier on the bite and hookset windows by quest band, applied in main.js after the forgiving first-quest window (quests 1–2 keep 1800/1200 ms). Windows only tighten after quest 5, never while the player is still learning; legend fights already ramp 3/4/5 by water in legendFight.

antiBurnout: Every quest introduces a new mechanic, unlock, water or legend — no quest is only more of the last one (see the quest table in docs/quests.md).
No quest is more than 70% idle waiting (target active share above); quest 11 is the one exception — a background collection quest at 30% active, flagged in the pacing log.
A quest with a target over 20 minutes is split or given a midpoint reward; quests 11 and 12 are the only 20-minute targets and both pay a completion bonus.
A first session reaches quest 2 and the first hand-fought catch within 10 minutes; if the pacing log shows otherwise, the early windows widen before any later quest is tuned.

economy.note: Coin values as shipped in main.js (idle +5, hand-fought +25, legend +100). Quest-completion bonuses are design TARGETS: quest completion is not wired in the game yet (in-game quest tracking is a placeholder — see docs/build-sheet.md), so no bonus is paid today; the bonuses below are what the milestone-4 shop pays when quest tracking ships.
economy.idleCoinsPerMinuteTarget: 25–30 (from the 4–9 s idle gap at a 60% auto-catch rate)
economy.activeCoinsPerMinuteTarget: About double the idle rate when the player hand-fights the big bites and completes quests, so active play is always worth more than leaving the line alone.

questCompletionBonusCoins.note: 25 coins times the quest number. Target only — see the note above.

economy.spending: Coins are spent only on tackle and lures in the milestone-4 upgrade shop (placeholder today); nothing costs real money, and no timer, energy or ad gate ever stalls the idle loop.
